title: The 5 Fastest Wingbeats in Nature, Ranked (Hummingbirds Barely Make It)

scenes.text: A hummingbird's wings are a blur. They only rank fifth.

scenes.label: Hummingbird · 80/sec
scenes.text: Number five: the bee hummingbird. About eighty wingbeats a second in normal flight, and up to two hundred in courtship.

scenes.label: Honeybee · 230/sec
scenes.text: Number four: the honeybee. Around two hundred to two hundred thirty beats a second, which makes that buzz.

scenes.label: Mosquito · 300-600/sec
scenes.text: Number three: the mosquito. Roughly three hundred to six hundred beats a second, depending on species.

scenes.label: Midge · 650-700/sec
scenes.text: Number two: the chironomid midge. Six hundred fifty to seven hundred beats every second.

scenes.label: Biting midge · 1,046/sec
scenes.text: Number one: a tiny biting midge. Over a thousand beats a second, over sixty-two thousand a minute. A record.

description:
The five fastest wingbeats in nature, measured in beats per second.
The record is a tiny midge at 1,046 beats per second, measured in 1947.
Which animal would you rank next?
first_comment: Did you guess a midge? Tell us which animal to rank next.
